items.bold: TRUMP: "They told me the CONCEPT OF THE DEAL. Waiting for the EXACT WORDING." — Most positive US signal of the war.
items.text: CNBC (1 hour ago) confirmed: Trump said on Saturday at West Palm Beach airport before boarding Air Force One to Miami: "They told me about the concept of the deal. They're going to give me the exact wording now." This is the most positive signal from the US since the war began February 28. Trump shifted from "not satisfied" (Friday) to "waiting for exact wording" (Saturday) — a significant softening. He also warned that there was still the "possibility of restarting strikes if Tehran misbehaves" and said "on a human basis, I don't prefer the military course." The concept being discussed: Iran opens Hormuz + ends war + no-restart guarantee, US lifts blockade. Nuclear talks deferred to later phase.

items.bold: IRAN SENIOR OFFICIAL (Reuters): Proposal is a "SIGNIFICANT SHIFT." Nuclear deferred — Iran demands right to peaceful enrichment.
items.text: Reuters (senior Iranian official, anonymity): Iran's latest proposal to shelve nuclear talks for a later stage was described as a "significant shift aimed at facilitating an agreement." Under the proposal: the war ends with a guarantee that Israel and the US would not attack again; Iran opens the strait; the US lifts its blockade; future talks would then address curbs to Iran's nuclear programme in return for lifting of sanctions. Critically: Iran demands Washington recognise its right to enrich uranium for peaceful purposes, even if it agrees to suspend its nuclear programme. This is Iran's bottom line on nuclear — not zero enrichment, but recognised peaceful enrichment with suspension. A significant difference from Trump's demand of full abandonment.

items.bold: US PCE inflation +0.7% March — war-driven energy feeding US inflation. Gasoline $4.30/gallon (+7 cents).
items.text: Time magazine (1 day ago) and CBS News confirmed: the US Personal Consumption Expenditure (PCE) price index rose 0.7% in March from February — the highest monthly increase in nearly two years — reflecting rising costs for goods and services as war-driven energy prices feed through to the US economy. National average gasoline climbed to $4.30 per gallon, up 7 cents from the previous day. The domestic US inflation from the war is now becoming a direct political pressure on Trump — gas prices above $4 hurt ordinary Americans, and every week of blockade raises the domestic political cost. This inflation pressure is accelerating Trump's incentive to reach a deal, even at the cost of deferring nuclear talks.

items.bold: TRUMP: Does NOT need congressional permission to extend war beyond May 1. Murkowski AUMF May 11 still pending.
items.text: CNBC (Reuters) confirmed: Trump told congressional leaders he does not need their permission to extend the war beyond the May 1 deadline set by law, because the ceasefire had "terminated" hostilities. This is the administration's legal theory: the ceasefire means there are no active hostilities, so the 60-day war powers clock does not apply. Democrats and some Republicans dispute this. GOP Sen. Murkowski (R-Alaska) still plans to introduce an AUMF measure when the Senate returns May 11 — forcing a Senate vote on formally authorising or ending the war. The AUMF threat is the next congressional pressure point. If Murkowski follows through, it puts Republicans in a difficult position: vote to authorise a war many find uncomfortable, or force its end.

assessment.body:
Sunday 6:15 AM IST. Day 65. The West Asia War's most positive diplomatic moment since the ceasefire.

THE TRUMP SIGNAL — "CONCEPT OF DEAL. EXACT WORDING."
• Trump (West Palm Beach, May 2, before Air Force One): "They told me about the concept of the deal. They're going to give me the exact wording now."
• Shift from Friday: "not satisfied" → Saturday: "waiting for exact wording"
• This is the most positive US signal since February 28
• He also warned: "still the possibility of restarting strikes if Tehran misbehaves"
• "On a human basis, I don't prefer the military course"
• Translation: diplomatic door is open — military option remains ready

THE IRAN PROPOSAL — FULL DETAIL (REUTERS)
• War ends with guarantee Israel and US will not attack again
• Iran opens the Strait of Hormuz
• US lifts its naval blockade
• Nuclear talks: deferred to later phase
• Iran demands: recognised right to enrich uranium for peaceful purposes
• Iran calls this a "significant shift aimed at facilitating an agreement"
• Gap with Trump's "full abandonment" demand: real but potentially bridgeable

WHY TRUMP IS MOVING — THE DOMESTIC PRESSURE
• US PCE inflation +0.7% March — highest in 2 years
• Gasoline: $4.30/gallon, up 7 cents in one day
• War cost: $25B (Pentagon) — senators say vastly understated
• November 2026 midterms approaching
• A deal that reopens Hormuz and lowers gas prices = massive political win

INDIA'S MONDAY MORNING
• Markets closed Fri (Labour Day) + Sat. Reopen Monday 9:15 AM IST
• Brent $108-110 (down from $126 Thursday peak)
• Trump "concept of deal" = most positive signal India's markets can receive
• 50%: Deal accepted → Nifty 24,200-24,500, Brent $88-96, rupee below 94
• 35%: Talks continue → Nifty cautious recovery 24,000-24,200
• 15%: Breakdown → Nifty below 23,000, Brent $135-145
• State election results May 4 = additional catalyst

VERDICT: Day 65 opens as the most diplomatically promising morning of the entire West Asia War. Trump's "concept of deal, waiting for exact wording" language is not rhetoric — it is the language of a negotiator who has received a proposal he can work with. Combined with Iran's senior official describing their proposal as a "significant shift," the pieces of a deal are closer than at any point since February 28. The question is whether the nuclear gap — Iran wants peaceful enrichment recognised, Trump wants full abandonment — can be bridged. If it can: Brent crashes $15-20 in a session, India's markets surge, the rupee strengthens, and the worst energy crisis in history begins its slow end. If it cannot: CENTCOM's "short and powerful" strikes plan is ready to execute.
